meta.title: Brown Act rules used by the agenda validator
meta.method: Section text read on leginfo.legislature.ca.gov on the verified_on date. 'verified' means the number or wording below was compared with that text. It does not mean an attorney has reviewed how the rule is applied here.

status_values.assumption: design choice or common practice, not statute text
status_values.not_modeled: statute exists but this demo does not check it

clocks.what: Agenda posted in a freely accessible location and on the agency website (if it has one) at least 72 hours before a regular meeting
Written notice received by each member (unless waived) and by media that asked for notice, at least 24 hours before the meeting; also posted on the website
Call and notice posted at least 24 hours before in a freely accessible location
Media that asked for special-meeting notice notified by phone (or email if they asked for email) one hour before an emergency meeting. This is a media notice, not a posting clock.
clocks.note: The research report called this a 1-hour posting clock.

clocks.what: For a dire emergency, media notified at or near the time members are notified
Minutes, list of persons notified, rollcall vote and actions posted for at least 10 days as soon after the meeting as possible

description.what: A brief general description of each item, including closed-session items. The description 'generally need not exceed 20 words'. This is a guideline on length, not a cap.

accommodation_notice.what: Agenda says how, to whom and when to ask for a disability-related modification or accommodation

special_meeting_pay_bar.what: No special meeting on salaries, salary schedules or fringe benefits of the legislative body or a local agency executive (budget discussion excepted)

quorum.what: Quorum is computed as a majority of all seats. Check the agency's enabling act or bylaws; some bodies count differently.

in_person.label: In person at the noticed meeting location

teleconf_posted.label: Traditional teleconference from a posted, public location
teleconf_posted.what: Each teleconference location is identified in the notice and agenda, is accessible to the public, and has the agenda posted. At least a quorum participates from locations inside the agency's territory.

ada_remote.label: Remote participation as a disability accommodation
ada_remote.what: Treated as in-person attendance at the physical meeting location for all purposes, including quorum-location rules. Audio and video required unless a disability-related physical condition requires off-camera participation. Member discloses any adults in the room before action is taken. Subdivision (b) and §§ 54953.8-54953.8.7 do not apply.

just_cause.label: Remote for just cause

grounds.c3: Physical or mental condition not covered by § 54953(c)

just_cause.what: At least a quorum participates in person from one physical location named on the agenda, open to the public and inside the agency's territory. Member gives notice with a general description, uses audio and video, and stays within the yearly cap. Minutes name the ground relied on.
just_cause.note: The research report said the AB 2449 rules ended on 12/31/2025. SB 707 re-enacted a just-cause track here, repealed 1/1/2030 by its own terms.

emergency_remote.label: Remote during a proclaimed state of emergency or local emergency
emergency_remote.what: Allowed during a proclaimed emergency to decide, or after deciding by majority vote, that meeting in person would present imminent risks. Findings renewed every 45 days. No physical public location required. Phone-only public access is allowed.

other_54953_8.label: Other § 54953.8 track (health authority, neighborhood council, student organization, subsidiary body, multijurisdictional body)
other_54953_8.what: §§ 54953.8.1, .8.4, .8.5, .8.6 and .8.7 each have their own conditions. This demo does not check them.

public_access.what: Public can hear, see and address the body remotely through a two-way audiovisual platform, or a two-way phone service plus a live webcast

agenda_access_notice.what: Agenda gives the call-in or internet option for attending and commenting

adults_disclosure.what: Remote member discloses, before any action, whether adults are in the room and the general relationship

minutes_listing.what: Minutes list each remote member and the provision relied on

standard.what: Using the § 54954.5 forms is optional. A body is not in violation of § 54954.2 or § 54956 if closed-session items were described in substantial compliance with § 54954.5, whatever the format.
standard.note: The research report said the descriptions must be exact. The text says substantial compliance.

forms.label: CONFERENCE WITH LEGAL COUNSEL—ANTICIPATED LITIGATION
forms.reminder: § 54956.9(e)(2)-(5) may require more facts on the agenda or in an oral statement before the closed session.

forms.label: THREAT TO PUBLIC SERVICES OR FACILITIES
forms.note: AB 2715 (Stats. 2024, ch. 243, effective 1/1/2025) added cybersecurity threats to critical infrastructure controls or information to § 54957(a). It did not amend § 54954.5, so there is no separate cybersecurity form; this is the existing § 54957 form.

closed_session_safe_harbors.not_modeled: Forms in § 54954.5(a), (g), (h), (i), (j) and (k) (license/permit, case review, trade secret and hospital hearings, federal-law complaints, joint powers agency, state audit) are not checked.

cure_and_correct.what: Written demand to cure within 90 days of the action, or 30 days if the action was in open session in violation of § 54954.2. The body has 30 days to respond.

social_media.what: A member may use public social media to inform or hear from the public, but a majority may not discuss agency business among themselves there, and a member may not respond directly to another member's post on agency business. SB 707 kept this rule in the section.
